    Most people build their investing rules out of their own mistakes. You hold something too long, you sell something too early, and you learn what a wash sale is sometime around the first week of April. Nobody hands you the rulebook in advance. You write it after the fact, usually at your own expense. Congress has the opposite arrangement. The people who write the country's financial rules also decide which of those rules apply to themselves, and for the past 14 years they have landed on the same answer, which is disclose rather than prohibit.
